Granny's cheese scones

Every Sunday when I was little, the kitchen smelled of these. My granny never wrote the recipe down, so after years of pestering I finally stood next to her with a notebook. Here it is, more or less.

What you need

  • 225g self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • a pinch of salt
  • 55g cold butter, cubed
  • 100g mature cheddar, grated
  • 150ml milk, plus a splash for brushing

How to make them

First, get your oven on to 220C (200C fan, gas 7) and grease a baking sheet. Granny used lard but butter is fine.

Mix the self-raising flour, baking powder and salt in a big bowl. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in most of the cheese, saving a little for the tops.

Pour in the milk and bring it together into a soft dough with a cutlery knife. Don't overwork it.

Pat the dough out on a floured surface to about 2cm thick and cut out rounds with a 6cm cutter. Put them on the sheet, brush with milk and sprinkle over the rest of the cheese.

Bake for 12-15 minutes until risen and golden. Cool on a wire rack, or eat warm with lots of butter.
